testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A cardboard box on the roadway:

options.text: May have a heavy object inside that could damage your vehicle.
Should be avoided by driving off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have a heavy object inside that could damage your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Any object on the road is dangerous. A cardboard box or paper sack that looks harmless could contain something hard or heavy that could seriously damage your vehicle.

questions.question: If another vehicle is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are being tailgated, create more space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can pass. Driving faster will not help. The other driver may just tailgate you at the higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air pressure can leak away over time. In an air brake system, emergency brakes must use mechanical force to stay engaged.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what counts as a look?

options.text: Getting out of your vehicle and walking to the back to check its position
Using side mirrors to check your vehicle's position
Looking out the driver's side window to check your vehicle's position
Glancing over your shoulder to check blind spots

questions.correctAnswerText: Getting out of your vehicle and walking to the back to check its position
questions.explanation: A look means you open your door, leave your seat, and walk to the back of your vehicle to check its position. During straight line backing, you can look only once. During other exercises, you can look twice.

questions.question: Front brake limiting valves were designed to:

options.text: Stop the front tires from skidding.
Prevent the front tires from overheating.
Use brake power equally on all wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes have front brake limiting valves to reduce the risk of front wheels skidding. Research has shown these valves are not needed, so they should be left in the normal position.

questions.question: In an emergency, if you must drive onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Steer so all wheels are on the shoulder.
Stop safely before getting back on the road, if possible.
Stay on the shoulder until the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely before getting back on the road, if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must drive onto the shoulder, keep one set of wheels on the pavement to maintain better control. If possible, let your vehicle come to a complete stop on the shoulder, then return to the road when it is safe.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: By tapping the brake pedal three times
By pushing in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: By pushing in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull the knob out to engage the parking brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: An air brake-equipped vehicle traveling at 55 mph under ideal conditions needs approximately ____ to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake-equipped vehicle traveling at 55 mph under ideal conditions needs about 450 feet to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what is the best way to check your lights?

options.text: Park near a mirror to see the reflection
Turn on the lights, then get out of the vehicle to look at them
Look at the instrument panel to see if warning lights are on
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to signal if your lights are out

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights, then get out of the vehicle to look at them
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, turn on your lights and get out of the vehicle to check that they work.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down?

options.text: Turn on the right turn signal followed by the left turn signal.
Tap your brake pedal a few times to light up your brake lights.
Swerve side to side to get other drivers' attention.
Turn all lights on and off several times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to light up your brake lights.
questions.explanation: To warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down, tap your brake pedal lightly a few times to make your brake lights flash.

questions.question: What is the problem with tires of different sizes?

options.text: They can be used on a tractor.
They can be used on a trailer.
They should be used in bad weather.
They should not be used on any vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should not be used on any vehicle.
questions.explanation: Tires of different sizes are a problem. They must be fixed if found during a vehicle inspection.

questions.question: At what air pressure does an air compressor governor stop pumping air into the tanks?
questions.explanation: An air compressor governor stops pumping air when the tanks reach 125 psi. This is called the cut-out level.

questions.question: What should you do if you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge?

options.text: Swerve as you pass under it.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle fits under something, slow down. Try to find a different route if possible.

questions.question: When a tire goes flat and makes a loud bang, when does the truck get affected?

options.text: Only if the flat tire is in the front.
Only if the truck is carrying cargo.

questions.explanation: There is a short delay between the sound of a tire failing and when the truck is affected. This delay may make the driver think the sound came from another vehicle.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, press down on the brake pedal.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a construction worker on the road?

options.text: Do not drive in any lane.
Wait until construction is finished before going.

questions.explanation: In work zones with workers on or near the road, you must reduce your speed.

questions.question: When should a low air pressure warning signal turn on?

options.text: When tank pressure drops below 120 psi.
When tank pressure drops below 60 psi.
When tank pressure drops below 10 psi.
When tank pressure drops below 5 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tank pressure drops below 60 psi.
questions.explanation: A low air pressure warning must turn on if air pressure in the tanks drops below 60 psi. The warning may be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: Where should placards be placed on a vehicle?

options.text: On the front, back, and both sides

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, back, and both sides
questions.explanation: For vehicles carrying hazardous materials, identical placards must be placed on the front, back, and both sides.

questions.question: Where can retreaded tires be used on a bus?

options.text: On the front of a bus.
On the rear of a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: What does driving intrastate mean?

options.text: Driving from one state to another

questions.explanation: Intrastate means you drive a commercial vehicle only within one state, and your cargo does not start or end outside that state.

questions.question: An applicant will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if they:
questions.explanation: Your hazardous materials endorsement can be denied or canceled if you are wanted for, under indictment for, or convicted of certain felonies. Other reasons include not having legal permanent status in the U.S., renouncing U.S. citizenship, being judged mentally incompetent, or being deemed a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration.

questions.question: If driving in fog, you should not:
questions.explanation: When driving through fog, slow down. Use your low beam headlights and fog lights. Turn on your four-way flashers. Do not increase your speed.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Cancel your signal once your turn or lane change is complete.
Don't signal unless another vehicle is close.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't signal unless another vehicle is close.
questions.explanation: Always signal before a turn or lane change. Signal early and keep it on during the entire turn. Turn it off when your turn or lane change is complete. Always signal, regardless of whether other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, drivers must check that it is secure every:
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement before you start driving, within the first 50 miles, and then every 150 miles or three hours.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle's lights before driving:

options.text: The vehicle should be running and in gear.
The engine should be turned off.
The check can be done from inside the vehicle.
The check can be done by looking at a reflection from a shiny surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine should be turned off.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and remove the key before checking lights. Set the parking brake. Turn on your low beam headlights and four-way flashers. Get out of the vehicle to check that all lights work properly.

questions.question: Always drive so your vehicle can stop:

options.text: Within 10 feet of your current position.
Within 1,000 feet of your current position.
Within your view of the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within your view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Drive at a speed that allows your vehicle to stop completely within the distance you can see ahead on the road.

questions.question: When traveling with cargo, you must check that it is secure:

options.text: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving.
Only after traveling up a hill.
Only after coming to a hard stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and every 150 miles or three hours of driving. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safely secured the entire trip.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, you should:

options.text: Keep the vehicle running while adding coolant.
Not use gloves to touch the radiator cap.
Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and let it cool before adding coolant. Use gloves or a thick cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release pressure.

questions.question: If your vehicle's ABS is not working while driving, you should:

options.text: Use your parking brake to stop.

questions.explanation: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working, your basic brakes still work. Continue to drive and brake normally.

questions.question: Cargo of hanging meat:

options.text: Is stable due to the placement of the load.
Can be problematic because animals may be attracted to the scent.
Is unstable due to its high center of gravity.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is unstable due to its high center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat cargo is unstable because it has a high center of gravity. The swinging motion of the meat can affect how you handle the vehicle. Drive with extra care when transporting this type of cargo.

questions.question: How does fatigue affect driving?

options.text: It has little effect on driving.

questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous and increases crash risk. Plan ahead and rest before long trips to avoid driving tired.

questions.question: If you get a traffic ticket in your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: The officer will tell your employer.
Your CDL will not be affected because it is on your personal license.
You should tell your employer within six months.
You must tell your employer within 30 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer within 30 days.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction, no matter what vehicle you were driving. Parking violations do not count.

questions.question: What happens if brakes get too hot?

options.text: The air compressor cools them down.

questions.explanation: If brakes overheat from heavy use, they can stop working. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: What condition should engine belts be in?
questions.explanation: Check engine belts to make sure they are tight and not worn. Each vehicle has different tightness requirements, so check your vehicle's manual.

questions.question: When does the safety valve on the first air tank open?
questions.explanation: The safety valve releases air if pressure gets too high, usually at 150 psi. If the valve opens, there is a problem with the system that needs repair.

questions.question: What can a modulating control valve control?
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets drivers apply spring brakes slowly and gradually. The lever is on the dashboard.

questions.question: What is another name for front end header boards?
questions.explanation: Front header boards are also called "headache racks." They protect the driver if cargo shifts during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: Which is NOT another name for convex mirrors?
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are called "fisheye," "spot," or "bug-eye" mirrors, but not "flat side mirrors."

questions.question: How do you prevent a manual transmission vehicle from rolling backward at a stop?

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
Place the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake to prevent rolling backward. Use the parking brake if needed.

questions.question: When spring brakes are activated, what should you never do?
questions.explanation: Never press the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. The combined force could damage the brakes.

questions.question: What are escape ramps?

options.text: Ramps to exit the interstate quickly.
Ramps that connect four-lane highways and two-lane highways.
Ramps that stop runaway vehicles on steep downhill slopes.
Ramps that cannot be used by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ramps that stop runaway vehicles on steep downhill slopes.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep hills to safely stop runaway vehicles. They have a long bed of loose, soft material and sometimes an uphill slope.

questions.question: What should you do before driving downhill?

options.text: Use only your brakes to slow down.

questions.explanation: On steep hills, use your engine to help slow the vehicle. Downshift before the hill. Relying only on brakes can cause them to overheat and stop working well.

questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid in some vehicles, what must you do?
questions.explanation: Some vehicles require the engine to be running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: When construction workers are near the road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: In construction zones, follow the posted speed limit. Slow down even more when workers are close to the road.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, when must you tell your employer?
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of a traffic conviction. Parking violations do not need to be reported.

questions.question: Why are roads extra slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Gravel washes to the middle of the lane.
Some tires are not made for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery at the start of rain. Water mixes with oil and grease to create a slick surface. As rain continues, the oil and grease wash away.

questions.question: What happens if engine belts are loose?

options.text: The water pump and fan do not work right, causing the engine to overheat.
The fan runs too much, making the engine too cold.
The belts last longer than tight belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water pump and fan do not work right, causing the engine to overheat.
questions.explanation: Check the belts in your engine. Loose belts will not turn the water pump and fan correctly, which can cause the engine to overheat.

questions.question: If you lose hydraulic pressure in your brakes, which should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: If your brakes lose hydraulic pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Look for an escape route like an escape ramp or side road. Do not speed up.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent tires and engine from overheating in hot weather?
questions.explanation: Driving faster makes your engine and tires hotter. In very hot weather, slow down to help prevent overheating.

questions.question: What is the problem with an underloaded front axle?

options.text: It is good because front axles are weak.

questions.explanation: An underloaded front axle can make it unsafe to steer your vehicle. Balance your cargo weight carefully.
